title: Cross-Disciplinary Integration of Quantum Computing in Economics and Finance
abstract_summary: This paper examines how quantum computing methods—notably quantum annealing, variational algorithms, and hybrid quantum–classical frameworks—can be applied to economic and financial modeling problems such as DSGE calibration, stochastic simulation, and systemic risk analytics. It emphasizes the role of university–industry partnerships in accelerating translational research, enabling scalable experimentation, and fostering data sharing and interdisciplinary education to support early adoption of quantum-enhanced decision sciences.
methodology_description: This is a conceptual and theoretical study that examines how quantum computing methodologies can be integrated into economic and financial modeling. The paper synthesizes and maps quantum algorithmic paradigms (notably quantum annealing, variational algorithms, and hybrid quantum–classical frameworks) onto specific modeling challenges in macroeconomics and finance, such as Dynamic Stochastic General Equilibrium (DSGE) modeling, large-scale stochastic simulations, and systemic risk analytics. The approach combines analytical reasoning about algorithmic advantages (e.g., solution-space exploration, improved tractability for high-dimensional optimization) with institutional analysis of university–industry collaboration mechanisms to accelerate translational research, scalable experimentation, data sharing, and interdisciplinary education. The methodology emphasizes comparative conceptual evaluation—identifying where quantum-enhanced algorithms could reduce computational bottlenecks—and proposes hybridized frameworks as pathways to bridge theoretical quantum advances with applied financial modeling. No empirical experiments, datasets, or hardware-based evaluations are reported; the work is positioned as a forward-looking integration and synthesis of prior theoretical and methodological advances.
